subject: ADR-189: settle before the first act, and say which -- the door stamps a page and waits for it to stop building (in the RISK READ as well as the act), and `stale` becomes a refusal of its own (protocol 1.6)
body: TWO MORE ADR-187 FINDINGS, ONE CAUSE: the door made the client do its bookkeeping. [data-h] is stamped by DISCOVER, which only observe ran, so three of four blind operators opened with a pick or an activate and were told the page had no control of that kind at all. _settle() stamps and waits for ADR-188's version digest to stop moving -- two consecutive readings that agree -- bounded at six rounds of 60 ms, once per DOCUMENT via window.__H_SETTLED; open and reload settle the document they arrive in and answer with its version. CRITICALLY it settles in risk_for too: the gateway asks for the risk BEFORE the act, so settling only in execute would have read the risk of an unbuilt page (every name answering to nothing, nothing raised) and then pressed whatever the name turned out to mean -- a destructive control pressed unraised on the first call of every session, with every check green. And `stale` is now its own code (protocol 1.6, mapped by the transport, counted as a refusal by the robot): invalid_argument means fix the call, not_found means look for another subject, stale means read again -- three instructions that were spelled one way. verify_contract 111 -> 115, verify_report 140 -> 148, mutate_contract 31 -> 35, mutate_report 89 -> 95. No page and no task was edited.
